transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-16
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Rivera (Redwood Solutions Eng); Michael Rhodes (Coppergate Head of Cloud Ops), Sara Lee (Security Architect), Daniel Wu (PM), Karen O'Neill (Compliance)

Summary: Weekly security/compliance check-in for the Coppergate pilot. Covered SSO tests, audit/log retention, SOC2 artifacts, KMS questions and next steps.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly pilot security sync for Coppergate, appreciate you taking the time. we have priya and jordan from the eng team, we'll run through items from last week and the SSO test plan.
[00:18] Michael (Coppergate): thanks alex, yep, quick note, karen and i joined late but we're here, want to make sure we get the audit log format nailed down.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): great, quick agenda: 1) SSO/SAML status 2) audit log schema and retention 3) data deletion / retention during pilot 4) SOC2 docs 5) KMS integration questions, ok?
[00:45] Sara (Security): sounds good, and also we had a couple questions about IP allowlisting and where logs are stored, whether they land in redwood cloud or forwarded to our splunk.
[00:58] Jordan (Redwood): yep short answer - logs can be exported; we can push to your syslog/s3 or you can pull via API. we'll share a sample, anonymized, of the audit events.
[01:12] Daniel (Coppergate): perfect. on SSO, we tried the metadata exchange yesterday, got a mismatched cert error, not sure if that's on our side or the metadata file.
[01:25] Priya: mmm i've seen that - often it's clock skew or the signing cert name mismatch. if you can share the raw XML we can look, we'll also send a step-by-step guide.
[01:41] Michael: ok i'll upload the raw metadata to the shared drive after the call.
[01:47] Karen (Compliance): quick question on retention: during the pilot we need logs kept for 90 days but anonymized PII removed after 7 days. is that possible?
[01:58] Alex: yes, the platform supports configurable retention and redaction at ingest. priya, can you confirm specific fields we can redact?
[02:06] Priya: sure - we can redact user identifiers, email addresses, full text of messages on request; we typically replace with stable pseudonyms if you want correlation without revealing PII. note: pseudonyms still count as identifiers for some policies, so we can also hash with a salt you control.
[02:28] Sara: is that salt customer-controlled? we prefer keys under our KMS.
[02:33] Jordan: we have two integration options: bring-your-own-KMS via customer managed keys (we support KMS integrations and HSM workflows) or use Redwood-managed keys. for compliance we often recommend BYOK (bring-your-own-key).
[02:48] Michael: great. can you confirm whether Redwood stores any plaintext training data or transcripts? the legal team flagged concerns about model fine-tuning during pilot.
[02:58] Alex: by default hosted inference logs are stored for telemetry and debugging; we offer a configuration to disable storage of request/response payloads, and we can enable ttl deletion. training/fine-tuning on customer data is not done without explicit consent and separate agreement.
[03:15] Karen: okay please include that statement in the security pack.
[03:20] Priya: will do. i'll add the wording and the configuration options in the doc.

--- Topics Deep Dive ---
[03:35] Priya: SSO specifics: our IdP metadata needs an AssertionConsumerService URL, and we support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. common issues: cert mismatch, time sync, and assertion encryption flags. also we support mapping attributes to RBAC roles via SAML attributes.
[03:58] Michael: we're using Okta. we've got an Okta app configured but the first-login failed with an error about missing nameid.
[04:06] Priya: ok you may need to map the nameid to Email (or persistent id). we'll provide the attribute map. for tests we suggest 3 users: admin, se, and viewer to validate role mapping.
[04:22] Daniel: can we toggle SCIM provisioning later? not necessary for pilot but for rollout yes.
[04:27] Jordan: yes scim is on the roadmap and supported via a separate integration. for pilot we recommend manual user lists or SSO with basic provisioning.

[04:40] Sara: back to audit logs - what fields are included by default?
[04:46] Jordan: default audit events include: request timestamp, API key or user id (if SSO), model used, route, token usage, response code, and event source. payloads are optional and can be withheld.
[05:05] Sara: format? json lines, syslog?
[05:09] Priya: we can export both - ndjson for API ingestion, or syslog/forwarding to splunk. we'll share an example file and event mapping.
[05:20] Michael: we need to validate chain of custody - does Redwood provide signed logs or any form of tamper evidence?
[05:28] Alex: we support log forwarding to your collector so you own the golden copy; additionally we have append-only storage options with retention plus exportable hashes if you need integrity proofs. i'll ask jordan to detail the export and hashing options.
[05:45] Jordan: yep i'll include a sample with sha256 hashes in the export pack.

[06:00] Karen: SOC2 - can we get a redwood SOC2 Type II summary and the contact for your auditor? our compliance team needs that to advance procurement.
[06:10] Alex: yes, we'll send the SOC2 summary and auditor contact. we can't share the full report without an NDA in most cases, but the summary and control matrix we can send right away.
[06:24] Karen: that's fine as long as we can see controls around encryption, access controls, and third-party risk.
[06:32] Alex: understood, will include.

[06:40] Priya: quick note on data residency - for the pilot you're on the us-east region; if you need EU residency later we can provision region-specific deployments or a private deployment.
[06:52] Michael: good to know, for now US is fine.

[07:00] Daniel: about retention windows - how easy is it to change retention mid-pilot if legal asks for longer?
[07:07] Priya: retention is configurable per-tenant. we can change config and reprocess indexes, though extending retention means we would need to confirm storage costs and any re-ingestion; shortening is immediate and data is TTL'd.
[07:23] Sara: does shortening create immediate deletion or soft-delete? we need proof of deletion for auditors.
[07:29] Jordan: deletion triggers backend job that removes full payloads and then purges indexes; we can provide deletion report (timestamps + objects removed) that you can store.

[07:45] Michael: about encryption at rest - you said BYOK is supported; do you support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS?
[07:54] Priya: yes all three. HSM-backed keys are supported via partners, and we can map the keys to tenant storage. we'll include a matrix in the KMS notes.

[08:06] Karen: any physical separation for pilot? like dedicated instances?
[08:11] Alex: for pilot we generally run on shared tenants but can provide dedicated capacity if required; dedicated implies reserved capacity and extra cost but gives isolated compute and storage. for compliance gating you might want dedicated.
[08:26] Michael: we'd like to run the pilot on a logically isolated tenant with separate storage buckets. is that doable?
[08:33] Jordan: yes we can spin a dedicated tenant for the pilot; we'll need a quick add-on to the POC scope and an approval route. john, sorry i mean michael, we'll follow up with estimated cost. (laughter)

[08:50] Daniel: small nit - earlier you mentioned we could disable payload retention; does that affect troubleshooting when we hit an error?
[08:59] Priya: yes without payloads we have limited debugging; but we can support ephemeral capture - enable for a window then auto-delete after X days. that way you still get root-cause analysis capability without long-term storage.

[09:15] Michael: great. next, legal asked whether Redwood performs any model training with pilot input. you said no but can you confirm policy and technical guard rails?
[09:24] Alex: policy is no training without explicit agreement. technically, inference only - no model parameter updates. logs used for quality monitoring are aggregated and anonymized; any retention for evals is opt-in and subject to contract terms.

[09:40] Sara: can you provide an example of the anonymization pipeline? we need to reproduce it in our review.
[09:46] Priya: yes - we'll add a flow diagram and example transforms in the security pack. it will show fields redacted, hashing with salt, and examples of NER-based PII removal.

--- timestamps jump ahead as topics wrap and clarifications occur ---
[18:12] Alex: okay to recap quick: 1) redwood sends SOC2 summary + auditor contact 2) priya/jordan send SSO guide + attribute map 3) priya to share anonymized audit log sample 4) jordan to prepare KMS BYOK notes 5) michael to confirm SSO test user list. any additions?
[18:32] Karen: please also send the deletion proof process and retention change log sample.
[18:40] Alex: noted. we'll include deletion report example.
[18:46] Daniel: one question on observability - will we be able to see per-route token cost and latency during pilot?
[18:53] Jordan: yes, the console shows token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and latency p50/p95. for pilot we'll provide limited dashboard access.
[19:06] Michael: can that dashboard forward alerts to our pager?
[19:10] Priya: we have webhook and pager integrations - we'll include config notes.

[19:22] Sara: small thing - for the audit log sample please remove any customer-identifying strings; anonymize hostnames.
[19:30] Priya: absolutely, anonymized and redacted prior to sharing.

[19:40] Alex: any blockers for the next week?
[19:44] Michael: no blockers, just need the docs and SSO fix; we'll test metadata and report results.
[19:51] Karen: procurement will likely need the SOC2 summary and the control matrix to proceed.

[20:00] Alex: ok we'll prioritize SOC2 and logs. before we close, quick alignment on timeline - next week same time for KMS deep-dive?
[20:08] Michael: yes that works.
[20:11] Jordan: i'll schedule and include an invite with pre-reads.

[20:20] Daniel: one more question - what about legal hold? if regulatory asks to keep data longer, how is that handled?
[20:28] Alex: we can implement legal hold by setting retention overrides and exporting to your archival buckets; that process will be part of the enterprise contract. we'll note it in the follow-up docs.

[20:40] Karen: please include a short blurb about encryption key rotation policy. our auditors will want rotation cadence and process.
[20:47] Priya: will include KMS rotation docs and typical cadence (90 days recommended) and emergency rotation procedures.

[21:00] Alex: ok let's do quick recap of action items aloud.
[21:06] Michael: go ahead.
[21:08] Alex: priya to send SSO guide and attribute map; priya/jordan to share anonymized audit log sample; jordan to prepare KMS matrix and BYOK notes; alex to send SOC2 summary and auditor contact; michael to confirm SSO test users; all noted with deadlines we've recorded.
[21:30] Sara: thanks all.
[21:33] Alex: thanks, we'll follow up in email with the security pack and invite for KMS deep-dive.
[21:40] Michael: bye everyone.

End of transcript.
